periods.analysis: Priority-1 response time opened the arc at 6.2 minutes, with no prior quarter for comparison, and stayed comfortably green against the <=7.0-minute target. That is the right starting position for a fast-growing coastal city: strong, but not something we treat as automatic. The summer load was real around Harborview Pier, Shoreline Parkway, and the Route 6 beach corridor, and the east/west post plan kept the first-due units moving. Dispatch QA also showed that the new CAD priority-code prompts were being used consistently on cardiac, weapons, and structure-fire calls.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the current four-zone deployment model and keep Rescue 3 staged east of Marina Cut during weekend peak hours through the next quarter. Extend the CAD priority-code audit to a 10-call weekly sample by shift so we preserve speed without weakening classification discipline or public trust.

periods.analysis: Response improved to 5.9 minutes, a quarter-over-quarter movement of -0.3 minutes from 6.2, and remained green. The improvement tracks with the October signal-preemption tune-up on Harborview Boulevard and the winter staffing bid that reduced uncovered relief windows at Station 2. We also saw fewer beach-access congestion conflicts, but the holiday retail corridor on Bayfront Avenue still required close dispatch sequencing. This is good operational work: measurable, explainable, and repeatable.
periods.recommendations: Lock in the signal-preemption timing package for Harborview Boulevard and run the same field test on Seacliff Avenue before the spring event season. Maintain the relief-staffing overlap at Stations 2 and 5, and require the watch commander to review any Priority-1 call over 7.0 minutes within 24 hours.

periods.analysis: The measure moved to 6.2 minutes, a quarter-over-quarter increase of 0.3 minutes from 5.9, but it remained green and below the <=7.0-minute target. The rise was expected after heavier rain events, drawbridge openings near Marina Cut, and several mutual-aid assists on the north county line. The important point is that crews absorbed those conditions without breaking the service standard. The February tabletop on simultaneous medical and fire incidents also helped clarify when Battalion 1 should rebalance units instead of waiting for automatic cover moves.
periods.recommendations: Continue the 24-hour exception review for calls above 7.0 minutes and add a rain-event tag in CAD so we can separate weather friction from staffing or routing issues. Extend Battalion 1 dynamic move-up authority during forecasted storm windows, with after-action notes filed by the next shift change.

periods.analysis: Priority-1 response time edged to 6.3 minutes, up 0.1 minutes from 6.2, and stayed green. Growth pressure is showing in the numbers, especially around the South Harbor multifamily permits and the school-afternoon traffic pulse near Alder Ridge. Still, the system held because dispatchers used the Closest Unit Recommendation screen and field supervisors kept EMS 4 from being pulled too far out of the central grid. A green quarter here means we are managing growth deliberately, not coasting through it.
periods.recommendations: Keep EMS 4 in the central grid from 1500 to 1900 on school days and document any exception approved by the duty chief. Extend the South Harbor construction traffic briefing to dispatch, police traffic units, and fire company officers every Monday until the lane closures are complete.

periods.analysis: The result improved to 6.2 minutes, a quarter-over-quarter movement of -0.1 minutes from 6.3, and remained green. That small improvement matters because it came during the highest visitor quarter, with festival calls at Harbor Green, beach rescues, and late-night waterfront activity. The temporary Medic 6 posting at Pier Lot C on Friday and Saturday evenings appears to have reduced cross-city travel for the most time-sensitive calls. We should recognize the work while staying disciplined: fast response only builds trust when it is paired with consistent triage and clear scene handoffs.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the Pier Lot C posting for peak visitor weekends and convert it into a written special-event deployment checklist. Extend dispatcher-event coordination by assigning one command-channel monitor for Harbor Green events expected to exceed 5,000 attendees.

periods.analysis: Response time improved again to 6 minutes, down 0.2 minutes from 6.2, and remained green. The new turnout-time dashboard in Stations 1, 3, and 6 helped supervisors spot preventable delays without turning performance management into finger-pointing. Holiday parade operations also benefited from pre-positioned crews at Civic Square and Bayfront Avenue, which kept units from being boxed in by closures. This is the kind of procedural improvement residents expect from an AA-rated city: practical investments, visible accountability, and no drama.
periods.recommendations: Keep the station turnout dashboards live and add Station 2 in January after the network switch replacement is complete. Formalize the Civic Square/Bayfront pre-positioning plan for parades, tree-lighting, and other permitted closures, with routes attached to each event permit.

periods.analysis: The measure rose to 6.2 minutes, a quarter-over-quarter increase of 0.2 minutes from 6, while still staying green against the <=7.0-minute target. The increase was modest and explainable: winter respiratory demand pushed EMS volume, and two Water Street water-main repair zones narrowed access to the west side for several weeks. Public Safety coordinated with Public Works on the Pipeline Renewal detours, and that coordination kept the response standard intact despite the disruption. I am satisfied with the control measures, but the water-main work remains a serious operational constraint until the renewal segments are fully restored.
periods.recommendations: Maintain the Pipeline Renewal detour map in CAD and require Public Works to update closures by 0600 and 1800 each day while Water Street work continues. Extend temporary west-side staging for Engine 5 during active trenching windows, and include response-time impacts in the weekly infrastructure coordination meeting.

periods.analysis: Priority-1 response time increased to 6.4 minutes, up 0.2 minutes from 6.2, and remained green. This is still within standard, but it is the second consecutive quarterly increase, so we should treat it as an early signal rather than a problem solved by the color green. Growth in the North Inlet subdivision, spring tourism, and continuing Pipeline Renewal constraints on Water Street and Lift Station 4 access all added minutes at the margin. Crews and dispatch are managing the conditions well; our job now is to prevent a gradual drift toward the 7.0-minute line.
periods.recommendations: Hold the green result by extending temporary west-side staging through the end of the Pipeline Renewal work package and measuring its effect separately from citywide response time. Add a North Inlet peak-hour post for Medic 2 on Thursday through Sunday evenings for 60 days, then review CAD travel-time data before making it permanent.
